name: PR review
job: Every pull request read against your team's own rules before anyone reviews it
intro: PR review reads the rules your team already wrote down, in AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, REVIEW.md and the like, and proposes the ones your reviewers keep asking for. Every push gets a round: each rule passed, broken or not checked, and findings on their lines. Small clean changes can merge by themselves.
does: A ledger on every push: each rule in scope passed, broken or not checked, and why. Never looked never looks like fine.
A finding is the same on every push: marked fixed in the commit that fixed it, and one you dismissed never comes back.
An inbox by who each pull request waits on, decided by code: your review, your merge, returned to you, merging by itself.

accounts.why: One shared GitHub connection for the Lemma: the repositories it reads, and where the Lemma check goes.

setup: Connect GitHub and pick the repositories. PR review reads their rule files from the default branch and proposes rules from the last 60 merged pull requests' review comments; nothing proposed is used until someone accepts it.
Say who posts on GitHub (the Lemma's bot, or each reviewer as themselves), whether the Lemma check and comments go on, and the GitHub logins of your team.
Merging by itself starts off. Watch first records what would have merged; turn it on when the record looks right.
Or look around with a sample team first: acme/api and acme/web, ten pull requests, made-up people.
